about.title: Cloverdale Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Cloverdale is a small city, but its shops along S Cloverdale Boulevard and N Cloverdale Boulevard, its wine-country tasting rooms, and its apartment and rental properties all see visitors every day — and a wet floor, broken step, or cracked walkway can turn a routine errand into an injury. California premises liability law asks a specific question after a fall: did the property owner know, or should they have known, about the hazard, and did they fail to fix it or warn you? Proving that notice element often comes down to details — how long a spill sat there, whether a mat was missing, whether lighting was poor. Surveillance footage and photos taken right after the fall can matter enormously, and they tend to disappear or get overwritten quickly. Our team can start gathering that evidence and evaluate what happened to you at no upfront cost.

whyChoose.title: Why Notice and Evidence Matter in Cloverdale Cases

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew or Should Have Known
items.desc: California law requires showing the property owner had actual or constructive notice of the hazard. We can help pin down how long the dangerous condition existed before you fell.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Cloverdale businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having evidence and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Bar Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you were partly responsible for the fall — your compensation is simply adjusted to reflect your share of fault.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Cloverdale?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a government entity — a city building or public sidewalk, for example — the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim notice, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I fell partly because I wasn't paying attention?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still pursue a claim even if you share some blame for the fall. Your final recovery would be reduced by your percentage of fault, but it wouldn't disappear entirely.

items.question: Does it matter that Cloverdale is a small city with limited businesses?
items.answer: Not really — the same premises liability rules apply whether a fall happens at a tasting room off Cloverdale Boulevard or a larger retailer near US-101. What matters most is documenting the hazard, getting witness information, and requesting any video before it's deleted.

items.question: Is there a cost to talk with an attorney?
items.answer: No. We offer a free case review, and we work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
